title: Engineering of ultra-small diagnostic nanoprobes through oriented conjugation of single-domain antibodies and quantum dots
protocol: Place 1 mmol of cadmium oxide, 3 mmol of 2-ethylhexanoic acid, and 2 ml of octadecene into a three-neck 25-ml round-bottom flask.
Heat the mixture to approximately 200°C for 10 min until cadmium oxide dissolves completely.
Cool the mixture to room temperature.
Add 6 ml of octadecene, 2 ml of oleylamine, and 100 mg of hexadecylphosphonic acid.
Equip the system with adapters for vacuum drying, argon flow, a thermocouple, and a magnetic stirring bar.
Heat the reaction mixture to 100°C and pump out to 5 mbar for 5 min under vigorous magnetic stirring.
Let the argon flow, and heat the mixture to 170°C.
Pump out the system and dry the reaction mixture at 170°C for 20 min under vigorous stirring.
Place 3 mmol of selenium powder into a glass tube.
Add 1 ml of octadecene to the selenium powder.
Seal the tube with Parafilm and blow with argon for 10 min.
Inject 4 mmol of trioctylphosphine into the solution with a syringe.
Blow the solution with argon for another 20 min until complete dissolution of selenium and formation of a clear viscous solution.
Heat the reaction mixture to 250°C under argon flow and vigorous stirring.
Inject the selenium solution into the reaction mixture with a syringe.
Maintain the temperature of the reaction mixture at 230°C.
Take an aliquot (approximately 0.1 ml) of the reaction mixture every 30 seconds.
Dissolve the aliquot quickly in 2 ml chloroform in an optical quartz cuvette.
Record the optical absorption and luminescence spectra with excitation wavelength set to 400 nm, spectral range from 420 to 650 nm, integration time of 0.1 s, and slit width of 3 nm.
Monitor the photoluminescence band shift due to growth of CdSe nanocrystals.
Stop heating when the blue photoluminescence band approaches 510 nm.
Quickly cool the reaction mixture to 100°C immediately after reaching 510 nm.
Inject cold benzene into the reaction mixture if necessary to speed up cooling.
Add 2 ml of oleylamine into the reaction mixture in the three-neck flask.
Stir the mixture under argon at 100°C for 10 min.
Place 3 mmol of zinc oxide, 7 mmol of ethylcaproic acid, and 3 ml of triethyleneglycol dimethyl ether into a 10-ml reaction tube.
Heat the mixture to 150°C to completely dissolve zinc oxide and obtain a clear solution.
Cool the solution to room temperature.
Place 2.5 mol of thiourea and 3 ml of triethyleneglycol dimethyl ether into another 10-ml tube.
Slowly heat to 100°C to completely dissolve thiourea.
Cool the solution to room temperature.
Mix together the solutions of zinc ethylcaproate and thiourea in one reaction tube.
Seal the reaction tube with Parafilm.
Purge the reaction tube with argon for 10 minutes at room temperature.
Heat the reaction mixture to 180°C under argon while stirring vigorously.
Inject the zinc salt and thiourea dissolved in triethyleneglycol dimethyl ether dropwise into the heated reaction mixture at a rate of about 1 ml/min.
Continue stirring the reaction mixture at 180°C for another 30 minutes after completing the injection.
Stop heating the reaction mixture and allow it to cool down to 70–80°C.
Add approximately 10 ml of isopropanol to the cooled reaction mixture.
Stir the reaction mixture containing isopropanol for 1–2 minutes without heating.
Transfer the suspension of core–shell nanocrystals into a 50-ml polypropylene centrifuge tube.
Centrifuge at 5000 rpm for 5 minutes to separate the solid phase from the mother solution.
Discard the supernatant and add 10 ml of chloroform to dissolve the solid phase completely.
Add 10 ml of methanol and centrifuge at 5000 rpm for 10 minutes.
Discard the supernatant, add a second portion of 10 ml chloroform to redissolve the nanocrystals.
Add another 10 ml of methanol and centrifuge at 5000 rpm for 10 minutes.
Discard the supernatant again, then add a third portion of 10 ml chloroform along with 200 mg of trioctylphosphine oxide to dissolve the mixture completely.
Obtain a clear solution after dissolution and proceed to store options A or B as instructed.
Dissolve 10 mg of nanocrystals (QDs) in 1 ml of chloroform.
Add 1 ml of methanol to the solution.
Wash by centrifuging at 14,000 rpm for 4 min.
Repeat washing two more times and dissolve the pellet in 1 ml of chloroform.
Add 200 µl of 10 mg/ml DL-Cystein solution in methanol dropwise to the QD solution until it becomes cloudy.
Sediment the QDs by centrifuging at 14,000 rpm.
Wash the QDs three times with methanol to remove excess unreacted Cys.
Dry the QDs under vacuum.
Dissolve the dry powder of QDs in Milli-Q water dropwise using a 1 M NaOH solution.
Sonicate the solution.
Filter the solution through 0.22-µm Ultrafree-MC microcentrifuge filters.
Add the methanol solution of DL-Cystein to the chloroform solution of QDs slowly and dropwise, controlling the aggregation state of the mixture.
Replace DL-Cys from the surface of QDs with thiol-containing polyethyleneglycol (PEG) derivatives.

Add 156 µl of a 150 mg/ml hydroxyPEG solution in pure water or a mixture of 25 µl of a 100 mg/ml aminoPEG solution and 140 µl of a 150 mg/ml hydroxyPEG solution to 1 ml of a 10 mg/ml pure-water solution of QDs conjugated with DL-Cys.
Incubate the samples overnight at +4°C.
Pre-purify the samples by centrifugation using Amicon Ultra-15 filter units (10 kDa cut-off).
Purify the samples from excess ligands by gel-exclusion chromatography on Sephadex-25 homemade columns.
Pass QD samples through a 0.1-μm filter.
Measure particle size distribution using dynamic light scattering at 25°C in a low-volume quartz batch cuvette.
Calculate the particle hydrodynamic size from diffusion times using the Stokes–Einstein equation.
Repeat measurements at least three times for each sample and at each value of intensity of scattering measurement (10 runs per measurement).
Record absorbance spectra.
Measure photoluminescence at λ_ex = 400 nm.
Store functionalized QDs at +4°C for up to 2 months until conjugation with antibodies.
Do not freeze the samples.
Immunize a young adult male llama subcutaneously on days 1, 30, 60, 90, and 120 with cells expressing the antigen (50 x 10^6 cells per immunization).
Collect sera 15 days before each injection to follow the immune response against the immunogen.
Take blood samples >100 ml 15 days after each of the last three immunizations.
Isolate peripheral blood mononuclear cells \(PBMCs) by discontinuous gradient centrifugation at room temperature.
Place 17 ml of Ficoll-Histopaque-1077 into each tube.
Centrifuge the tube for 30 s at 840g at room temperature to force the medium through the porous barrier.
Remove excess ficoll from above the barrier, ensuring no air is left under the barrier and the surface of the medium and the barrier are at the same level.
Dilute blood twofold in PBS.
Place 30 ml of diluted blood into each tube containing Ficoll-Histopaque-1077.
Centrifuge the tubes at 400g for 40 min at room temperature without using a brake for deceleration.
Recover lymphocytes concentrated in the interphase between the plasma and separation solution.
Wash the recovered lymphocytes twice with PBS containing 1% FCS by centrifugation at 1500g for 20 min at room temperature.
Store the lymphocyte pellet at –80°C until RNA extraction.
Immunize llamas with the antigen of interest.
Recover peripheral blood mononuclear cells from blood using density gradient centrifugation (ficoll).
Amplify a pool of cDNA coding for sdAb genes by RT–PCR from total RNA preparation and clone into a phagemid vector.
Use a helper phage to produce a library of phage particles carrying sdAbs on their surface by fusion to the minor coat protein p3.
Enrich the phage-sdAb library with binders through incubation with immobilized antigen, followed by washing and elution.
Identify binders using a monoclonal screening assay.
Produce soluble sdAbs corresponding to positive phage–sdAbs from E. coli and analyze by SDS–PAGE.
Extract lymphocyte RNA using the GenElute Mammalian Total RNA Miniprep Kit (Sigma Aldrich) according to manufacturer recommendations.
Check extracted RNA on 2% agarose gel.
Store RNA at –80°C until construction of the library.
Put 1 µl of RNA mix, 1 µl of the 3'CH2-2 primer, and 13 µl of H2O DEPC into an RNase-free Eppendorf tube.
Incubate for 5 min at 65°C.
Cool down on ice.
Add 4 µl of the reverse transcriptase buffer.
Add 0.5 µl of RNAsine.
Add 2 µl of 10 mM dNTP mix.
Add 0.5 µl of reverse transcriptase.
Incubate for 30 min at 55°C.
Incubate for 5 min at 85°C.
Cool down on ice.
Perform PCR amplification using the primer 3'CH2-2 (0.05 µM) and the 5'VHx Sfi mixture (0.1 µM).
Mix each reaction with 4 µl of cDNA, 1× Phusion HF buffer, 200 µM dNTPs, primers, and 1 U of Phusion enzyme.
Heat the mixture for 3 min at 94°C.
Follow with 40 cycles consisting of denaturation at 94°C (1 min), annealing at 65°C (1 min), and elongation at 72°C (1.5 min).
Heating for 10 min at 72°C to complete elongation.
Check the results of PCR on a 2% agarose gel.
Store the product at –20°C.
Isolate the genes of IgG2 and IgG3 on agarose gel.
Purify DNA from isolated genes using a NucleoSpin Extract II column.
Mix 0.8 μl of first PCR product with Dynazyme buffer, dNTPs, primers, and Dynazyme II enzyme in a reaction mixture of 200 µl volume.
Heat the mixture for 3 min at 94°C.
Perform 30 cycles of denaturation at 94°C (30 s), annealing at 65°C (30 s), and extension at 72°C (1 min).
Heating the mixture for 10 min at 72°C for final extension.
Check the PCR product on a 2% agarose gel.
Purify the PCR product using a NucleoSpin Extract II column.
Elute the purified PCR product in a final volume of 30 µl.
Digest the entire PCR product for 3 h with BglI and NotI restriction enzymes following manufacturer recommendations.
Purify the digestion product on a NucleoSpin Extract II column and elute in a final volume of 20 µl.
Check the digestion on 2% agarose gel.
Digest 5 μg of vector with NotI and SfiI enzymes following manufacturer recommendations.
Purify the digestion product on a NucleoSpin Extract II column and elute in a final volume of 200 µl.
Check the digestion on 1% agarose gel.
Dephosphorylate the vector with Antarctic phosphatase following manufacturer recommendations.
Purify the dephosphorylated product on a NucleoSpin Extract II column and elute it in a final volume of 40 µl.
Use a fivefold molar excess of the insert over the vector.
Use 80 ng of vector and 40 ng of insert in a final volume of 10 µl for ligation reaction.
Add T4 DNA ligase (3 U) and enzyme buffer according to manufacturer's recommendations.
Perform a negative control without the insert.
Incubate overnight at 16°C.
Inactivate the DNA ligase by incubating at 65°C for 20 min.
Use 2 µl of ligation product and 25 µl of TG1 electrocompetent cell suspension per electroporation.
Plate transformation product onto 2× TYAG agar plates containing BCIP.
Calculate diversity obtained with one electroporation.
Perform enough electroporations to reach a minimum diversity of 10^6.
Keep 10 µl of the electroporation pool for titration.
Centrifuge the rest at 3000g for 10 min.
Resuspend the pellet in 2 ml of 2× TYAG.
Plate 500 µl of the bacteria suspension onto four 2× TYAG agar plates.
Grow overnight at 37°C.
Resuspend the colonies in 2.5 ml of 2× TYAG by scraping them with a spatula from six 2× TYAG agar plates and place them in a fresh test tube.
Spin at 3000g for 10 min.
Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the cells using a volume of 2× TYAG equivalent to the pellet volume.
Add glycerol to a final concentration of 15%.
Mix and store at –80°C.
Use the electroporation product pool to perform serial dilutions.
Add 10 µl of the pool to 995 µl of 2× TY \(a 10–2 dilution).
Make serial dilutions of the pool to a dilution of 10–8.
Plate 100 µl of each dilution of the bacteria suspension onto 2× TYAG agar plates.
Grow the cells overnight at 37°C.
Count the colonies and calculate the CFU or CFU/ml titer according to the dilution.
Inoculate 2× TYAG medium with a representative aliquot of your library.
Use 10 to 100 times more bacteria compared to the library diversity to avoid loss of diversity.
Grow the culture while shaking at 250 rpm at 37°C until the OD600 reaches 0.5.
Add KM13 helper phage to reach a ratio of 10–20 helper phages per cell.
Incubate without shaking at 37°C for 30 min.
Spin at 3000g for 10 min.
Resuspend the pellet in a volume of 2× TYAK five times larger than the initial volume.
Grow the culture while shaking at 250 rpm at 30°C overnight.
Centrifuge the bacterial culture in a 50-ml test tube at 3000g for 15 min.
Transfer 25 ml of the supernatant to a fresh test tube containing 1/5 the volume of PEG/NaCl.
Mix by inversion and incubate for 1 h on ice.
Centrifuge for 15 min at 3000g at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in 1 ml of cold PBS and transfer to a 1.5-ml Eppendorf tube.
Centrifuge for 5 min at 14,000g.
Transfer the supernatant to a fresh test tube containing 1/5 the volume of PEG/NaCl.
Mix by inversion and incubate for 20 min on ice.
Centrifuge for 5 min at 14,000g at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in 1 ml of cold PBS containing 15% glycerol.
Coat epoxy beads with antigen according to the manual.
Prepare an overnight preculture from a fresh colony of TG1 in 3 ml of 2× TY.
Incubate the overnight culture at 37°C.
Wash the immobilized antigen two or three times with TPBS and two or three times with PBS.
Saturate the antigen-coated material and 1012 phages of your library for 1–2 h at room temperature in MPBS.
Keep 10 µl of this phage suspension for titration (input).
Remove the MPBS and add preblocked phage to the blocked antigen.
Incubate for 2 h at room temperature while shaking gently.
Wash the beads nine times with TPBS and two times with PBS.
Elute the phage by resuspending the cells in 500 µl of trypsin (10 µg/ml) in PBS for 30 min at room temperature on a rotator.
Add 500 µl of PBS to the eluted material, bringing the final volume to 1 ml corresponding to the output of the selection.
Keep 10 µl of the eluted phage for titration.
Dilute the output phage suspension with 4 ml of 2× TY.
Add 5 ml of TG1 at OD600 = 0.5.
Incubate without shaking at 37°C for 30 min.
Spin at 3000g for 10 min.
Resuspend the pellet in 3 ml of 2× TYAG.
Plate 500 µl of the bacteria suspension on six 2× TYAG agar plates (15-cm Petri dishes).
Grow the culture overnight at 37°C.
Resuspend colonies in 2.5 ml of 2× TYAG by scraping them from six 2×TYAG agar plates and place them into a fresh test tube.
Centrifuge at 3000g for 10 min.
Resuspend the cells using one pellet volume of 2× TYAG.
Add glycerol to a final concentration of 15%.
Mix and store at –80°C.
Add 5 µl of each input phage suspension to 495 µl of 2× TY for a 10⁻² dilution.
Make serial dilutions of the phage suspension, reaching a final dilution of 10⁻¹² for the input and 10⁻⁸ for the output.
Inoculate each diluted phage suspension with 500 µl of TG1 culture at OD₆₀₀ = 0.5.
Incubate the inoculated suspensions without shaking at 37°C for 30 min.
Plate 100 µl of each bacterial suspension dilution onto 2× TYAG agar plates (9-cm Petri dishes).
Grow the plated bacteria overnight at 37°C.
Count colonies and calculate CFU or CFU/ml titer according to the dilutions.
Fill each well of a 96-well U-bottom polypropylene microtiter plate with 150 µl of 2× TYAG.
Inoculate 94 desired panning round clones into separate wells using sterile tips, leaving two wells as negative controls without clones.
Incubate the cultures overnight in a microtiter plate shaker at 37°C at 900 rpm.
Add glycerol solution to the overnight culture to achieve a final concentration of 15%.
Mix cell suspensions and store the master plate at –80°C.
Enzymatically detach adherent cells using a Trypsin–EDTA solution.
Add medium containing 10% (v/v) serum to inhibit trypsin and prevent further proteolytic degradation of surface molecules.
Count the cells, determining vitality by trypan blue exclusion staining if necessary.
Centrifuge the cells for 5 min at 300g at 4°C.
Resuspend the sedimented cells in 10 ml of cold PBS.
Centrifuge the resuspended cells again for 5 min at 300g at 4°C.
Use 10–50 x 10^6 of each cell type at the next step.
Saturate antigen-positive cells by incubating with 5 ml of MPBS for 1 hour on a rotator at 4°C.
Centrifuge the cells for 5 minutes at 300g at 4°C.
Add 10^12 phage–sdAb (blocked with MBPS) to the pelleted cells.
Incubate the mixture for 2 hours at 4°C on a rotator.
Pellet the cells by centrifugation for 5 minutes at 300g at 4°C.
Transfer the supernatant to a fresh test tube.
Wash the cells with 1 ml of PBS.
Centrifuge the cells for 5 minutes at 300g at 4°C.
Repeat the washing procedure 9 more times, ensuring all steps are performed at 4°C.
Fill a 96-well U-bottom polypropylene microtiter plate with 150 µl of 2× TYAG.
Add 5 µl of glycerol culture from the master plate to each well.
Incubate at 37°C with a breathable sealer in a microtiter plate shaker at 900 rpm until an OD600 of 0.5 is reached, approximately 1.5 h for fresh cultures or 2.5 h for frozen cultures.
Add helper phage M13KO7 to achieve a ratio of 10–20 helper phages per cell.
Incubate the cells without shaking at 37°C for 30 min.
Centrifuge the suspension at 350g for 10 min.
Resuspend the pellet in 150 µl/well of 2× TYAK.
Grow the culture overnight in a microtiter plate shaker at 30°C at 900 rpm.
Centrifuge the 96 well U-bottom polypropylene microtiter plate at 350g for 10 min.
Centrifuge adherent cells to obtain a suspension of separate cells.
Add medium containing 10% serum to inhibit trypsin and prevent further proteolytic degradation.
Count cells using trypan blue exclusion staining to determine cell vitality.
Sediment the cells by centrifugation for 5 min at 300g at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant completely.
Saturate cells and V-bottom microtiter plates with 5% MPBS for 1 h at 4°C.
Resuspend the cells at a concentration of 2x10^6 cells/ml.
Place the cell suspension into V-bottom microtiter plates using 100 μl per well.
Centrifuge the cells for 5 min at 300g at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant completely immediately after centrifugation.
Put the microtiter plate on ice.
Resuspend cells in 80 µl of 5% MPBS and 20 µl of phage–antibody solution per well.
Incubate for 2 h at 4°C while mixing gently.
Wash cells three times with 150 µl/well of PBS (add PBS, mix cells, centrifuge the suspension, discard the supernatant; repeat three times).
Put the microtiter plate on ice.
Resuspend cells in 50 µl per well of anti-M13-HRP monoclonal antibody.
Incubate for 1 h at 4°C while mixing gently.
Wash cells three times with 150 µl/well of PBS (add PBS, mix cells, centrifuge the suspension, discard the supernatant; repeat three times).
Resuspend cells in 100 µl/well of staining solution (18 ml of PBS, 1 ml of 1 M sodium citrate, 1 ml of 1 M citric acid, 20 µl of 30% H₂O₂, and one pastille of ABTS).
Engineer an extra C-terminal cysteine to facilitate sdAb conjugation using linear amplification with primers 6hisCysfor and 6hisCysrev.
Prepare each reaction mixture (25 µl) containing 50 ng of the vector, 1× PCR buffer, 200 µM dNTPs, 150 ng of each primer, and 1.25 U of Pfu Ultra DNA polymerase.
Heat the mixture for 30 seconds at 95°C.
Perform 25 cycles consisting of denaturation at 95°C (30 s), annealing at 55°C (1 min), and elongation at 68°C (2 min per kilobase).
Treat 9 µl of the reaction with 1 µl of DpnI solution for 2 hours at 37°C to digest the methylated parental plasmid.
Purify DNA by precipitation with absolute ethanol and washing with 70% ethanol.
Electroporate the purified DNA into electrocompetent XL1-blue cells following the manufacturer's instructions.
Check clones by DNA sequencing.
Electroporate pET sdAb–his6Cys vectors into E. coli strain Bl21DE3.
Inoculate the transformed cells in 10 ml of 2× TYAG medium.
Grow the inoculated cultures overnight at 37°C (250 rpm).
Dilute the cultures to an OD600 of 0.1 in 400 ml of fresh 2× TYA.
Grow the diluted cultures until the OD600 reaches 0.5.
Induce sdAb expression by adding 0.1 mM IPTG.
Incubate the cells at 30°C while shaking at 250 rpm for 20 hours.
Freeze the cell pellet for 20 minutes at -80°C.
Lysate the frozen cells by adding 20 ml of BugBuster and incubating gently for 20 minutes.
Purify proteins using Talon™ metal affinity resin according to manufacturer’s instructions.
Concentrate purified proteins in PBS with VIVASPIN 20 PES 5 kD.
Store concentrated proteins at -20°C.
Evaluate protein purity by SDS–PAGE analysis.
Determine protein concentration spectrophotometrically using a protein assay kit.
Prepare a 10 mM stock solution of TCEP in 50 mM phosphate buffer (pH 7.0) immediately before use.
Dilute an sdAb sample to obtain a 100 µM solution in 50 mM phosphate buffer, pH 7.0.
Add a tenfold molar excess of TCEP and incubate the mixture for 30 min at room temperature.
Use PD MiniTrap G-25 desalting centrifugation columns to remove the TCEP products and concentrate the sdAb–SH.
Use the sample of reduced sdAb–SH for conjugation with QDs immediately.
Dilute water-soluble QDs containing 10% aminoPEG and 90% hydroxyPEG to obtain a 4 mg/ml solution in 100 mM phosphate buffer, pH 7.2.
Add a 100-fold molar excess of Sulfo-SMCC to the diluted QD preparation.
Incubate the mixture for 1 hour at room temperature in the dark while stirring gently at 40 rpm on an RM-2L Intelli-Mixer.
Purify the maleimide-activated QDs by applying them onto a Sephadex G-25 resin column equilibrated with 100 mM phosphate buffer, pH 7.2.
Mix the purified maleimide-activated QDs with sdAb-SH to obtain a molar ratio of 1:10.
Incubate the mixture for 2 hours at room temperature in the dark while stirring gently at 40 rpm on an RM-2L Intelli-Mixer.
Purify the sdAb-QD conjugates by gel exclusion chromatography on a Superdex 200 resin column equilibrated with 100 mM phosphate buffer, pH 7.2.
Prepare the working solution of the PMPI crosslinker in DMSO.
Dilute water-soluble QDs containing only hydroxyl groups to obtain a 2 mg/ml QD solution in 50 mM sodium borate buffer, pH 8.5.
Add a 50-fold molar excess of PMPI to the QD sample.
Incubate the reaction mixture for 30 min at room temperature in the dark while stirring gently (40 rpm) on an RM-2L Intelli-Mixer.
Purify maleimide-activated QDs by applying the reaction mixture onto a home-made column packed with Sephadex G-25 resin and equilibrated with 50 mM phosphate buffer, pH 7.0.
Mix purified maleimide-activated QDs with sdAb-SH to obtain a molar ratio of 1:10.
Incubate the mixture for 2 h at room temperature in the dark while stirring gently (40 rpm) on an RM-2L Intelli-Mixer.
Purify the sdAb-QD conjugate by gel exclusion chromatography on a home-made Superdex 200 resin column equilibrated with 50 mM phosphate buffer, pH 7.0.
Use freshly prepared samples of sdAb-SH and solution of the PMPI crosslinker.
The prepared conjugates can be kept at +4°C.
Label cells with sdAb-QD conjugates for cell labeling.
Conduct flow cytometry measurements on labeled cells.
Suspend MC38 and MC38CEA cells by gently shaking for 5 min.
Wash 3 ∙ 10^5^ cells.
Incubate washed cells in the dark with different dilutions of sdAb–QD conjugates in PBS or human serum for 30 min at 4°C.
Wash cells twice with PBS containing 1% bovine serum albumin \(BSA).
Perform flow cytometry measurements of stained cells using a FACStar Plus or Guava EasyCyte™ Plus flow cytometer.
Excite the samples with a 488-nm argon laser and measure fluorescence intensity in the specified range for each instrument.
Collect at least 5000 events for each sample.
Use geometric mean fluorescence \(GMF) intensity channels to quantify staining of each sample.
Deparaffinize 5-μm paraffin sections in xylene.
Rehydrate sections through ethanol (100%, 96%, and 70%).
Bring sections to water.
Incubate slides for 60 min in a citrate buffer solution at 95°C.
Allow the slides to cool and incubate them in the same buffer at room temperature for 20 min.
Quench endogenous peroxidase activity by incubating slides with 3% hydrogen peroxide and 20% methanol.
Wash slides with water.
Block nonspecific binding by a 20-min incubation of tissue sections in a 2% solution of BSA in PBS containing 0.05% Tween 20.
Stain the tissue section with a 1.5 x 10^-8 M solution of anti-CEA sdAb-QD570 conjugates for 1 hour in a humidified chamber at room temperature.
Wash three times with PBS.
Observe fluorescence emission under a fluorescence microscope using 350–400 nm UV excitation and 450-nm (long pass) emission filters.
Apply a 1.6 x 10^-9 M solution of anti-CEA monoclonal antibody (clone TF3H8) to the tissue section for 1 hour in a humidified chamber at room temperature.
Wash it three times with PBS.
Stain the tissue with polyclonal goat anti-mouse IgG conjugated with FITC for 1 hour at room temperature.

After washing three times with PBS, mount the slides with mounting medium and view them under a fluorescence microscope using a 420- to 490-nm excitation filter and a 520-nm (long pass) emission filter.
Incubate the slides with anti-CEA monoclonal antibody (clone TF3H8-1, 6 x 10^-9 M) for 1 hour in a humidified chamber at room temperature.
Wash the slides with PBS and incubate them with biotinylated sheep anti-mouse polyclonal IgG in PBS at room temperature for 1 hour.
Develop the slides using a REAL™ system kit (peroxidase/DAB).
After washing with PBS-Tween, view the slides under an optical microscope.
